question: Why is a topical retinoid considered the backbone of most acne treatment plans, in terms of the four pillars of pathogenesis?

answers.text: It directly corrects follicular hyperkeratinisation — dissolving existing comedones and preventing new microcomedones at the source of acne pathogenesis

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Topical retinoids normalise the abnormal cohesion and retention of follicular keratinocytes, dissolving existing comedones and — crucially — preventing the formation of new microcomedones, thus halting acne at its structural origin. This makes a retinoid valuable across all grades of acne, from comedonal to inflammatory.

answers.text: It is the only topical agent that directly kills Cutibacterium acnes

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Retinoids do not directly kill C. acnes. The antimicrobial pillar is targeted by benzoyl peroxide (bactericidal via oxidation) and antibiotics (topical and oral). Retinoids target the hyperkeratinisation pillar — the plugging that initiates every acne lesion.

answers.text: It is the only agent that significantly reduces sebum production

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Topical retinoids do not meaningfully reduce sebum production. Sebum suppression is the domain of oral isotretinoin (which targets all four pillars) and hormonal agents such as combined oral contraceptives and spironolactone. Topical retinoids correct follicular keratinisation, not sebaceous output.

answers.text: It has no irritant side effects and is therefore universally tolerable

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Topical retinoids commonly cause irritation, dryness, and a transient initial 'purge' (apparent worsening). Tretinoin is also photodegradable and photosensitising, requiring night-time application and daytime sunscreen. These are manageable with proper counselling, but retinoids are certainly not free of side effects.

overallFeedback.feedback: Map each drug class to its pathogenetic pillar: retinoids → hyperkeratinisation (the backbone), BPO/antibiotics → C. acnes, isotretinoin → all four, hormonal agents → sebum.
Well done. Retinoids are the backbone because they uniquely target follicular hyperkeratinisation — the initiating structural event of every acne lesion.
